entities.text:
Secretary To Government,
 Government Of Puducherry
entities.label: PETITIONER

sentences.text: O R D E R
Delay condoned.
Leave granted.

This appeal by the Secretary, Government of Puducherry and another, takes exception to the judgment dated 18.01.2018 passed in W.A. No. 1102 of 2016 and C.M.P. No. 14271 of 2016, whereby the appeal preferred by the appellants herein was dismissed, with the direction that the respondent,
Alphonse Abichegaradjou, would be entitled to compensation under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 20131.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 20131
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The admitted facts are; that the land in question, 0.03.25 hectares in Survey No. 258/2A/1C in village Thattanchavady, Puducherry, became subject matter of notification issued on 28.07.1995 vide G.O.Ms. No. 65 under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 18942.

The respondent had,
thereupon, filed a writ 1 For short, 2013 Act.
2 For short, 1894 Act.
petition sometime in the year 1995 (exact date is not available on record, and the learned counsel for the parties are unable to state the actual date) challenging the acquisition proceedings.
An interim order restraining the appellants from dispossessing the respondent of the land was passed.

The writ The Secretary To Government vs Alphonse Abichegaradjou on 16 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120900225/
1 petition was dismissed on 18.08.2000.

entities.text: Secretary To Government vs Alphonse Abichegaradjou
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thereafter, possession of the land was taken by the appellant on 21.08.2000, and the award dated 26.12.2000 was passed.
It is to be noted that the land in question has been recorded in the name of one Babu.
The respondent claims that he is the grandson of Babu and has inherited the land along with others.
The respondent, however, is unable to produce any document or order to show lineage and inheritance and title, as well as the proportion/ percentage of the inheritance.

The respondent had challenged the orders passed by the High Court rejecting the challenge to the acquisition proceedings before this Court in SLP (C) No. 789 of 2015, which was dismissed on 20.04.2015.

The order dismissing the writ petition records that the respondent therein, i.e. the appellant before us, should refer the issue of enhancement of compensation to the appropriate authority at the earliest.
It is stated by the learned counsel for the appellants that some legal representatives of Babu have been paid the compensation.

The Constitution Bench of this Court in Indore Development Authority vs. Manohar Lal and Others,
(2020) 8 SCC 129, in paragraph 366.7, has held that once possession has been taken, there is no lapse of proceedings under the 1894 Act.

entities.text:
Indore Development Authority vs. Manohar Lal and Others,
(2020) 8 SCC 129
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the aforesaid legal position, the appeal is allowed and the impugned judgment holding that the provisions of 2013 Act would apply is set aside and quashed.
1894 Act would apply.

However, we clarify that the claim of the respondent on account of inheritance has not been examined by us and it will be open to the respondent to raise the said claim before the authorities in appropriate proceeding, who will decide the same expeditiously and as early as possible.
Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
